title: Basic Concepts
outcomes: Describe the components of income-tax law and the transition to the 2025 Act.
Apply the charge of tax, tax year and key definitions.

meta.exam_tip: State the regime first; compute slab tax, rebate, surcharge, cess in that order.

concepts.title: Components of income-tax law and the 2025 Act
body: Article 265 of the Constitution requires taxes to be levied only by authority of law; Parliament taxes income other than agricultural income under Entry 82 of the Union List.

From 1 April 2026, income-tax is governed by the Income-tax Act, 2025 (23 chapters, 536 sections, 16 schedules), which replaced the Income-tax Act, 1961. Under section 536 (repeal and savings), proceedings, rights, assessments and appeals for tax years beginning before 1 April 2026 continue under the 1961 Act, while carried-forward losses, MAT/AMT credit and certain deductions continue subject to conditions.

Other components: the annual Finance Act (rates in its First Schedule — Part IB for the current tax year, Part II for TDS, Part III for salary TDS and advance tax under the optional regime, Part IV for agricultural income), Income-tax Rules, 2026, notifications and circulars (binding on the department), and case laws.
concepts.analogy: The 2025 Act is the new law; the 1961 Act still governs older years.
concepts.work: An assessment for T.Y. 2025-26 continues under the 1961 Act.

concepts.title: Rules of interpretation
body: Rules of interpretation help courts find the lawmakers' intention. Literal rule: clear words are given their plain meaning. Mischief (Heydon's) rule: read the law to suppress the mischief it was meant to cure. Golden rule: depart from literal meaning only to avoid absurdity.

Harmonious construction reconciles conflicting provisions; beneficial provisions are read liberally; taxing provisions are construed strictly, with doubts resolved in favour of the assessee; procedural provisions may operate retrospectively.
Internal aids (definitions, explanations, provisos, headings) and external aids (speeches, committee reports, circulars) also assist interpretation.
concepts.analogy: Courts read tax law strictly but sensibly.
concepts.work: An ambiguous charging provision is resolved in the taxpayer's favour.

concepts.title: Charge of tax, tax year and key definitions
body: Section 4 is the charging section: every person's total income for a tax year bears income-tax at the rates fixed by the Finance Act or by the Act itself (for example section 202(1)), subject to its other provisions.

Tax year (section 3) is the twelve-month financial year beginning 1 April; for a new business or source, it runs from setting up or commencement to 31 March. Income of a tax year is assessed after it ends, except for non-resident shipping, persons leaving India, AOPs formed for a particular event, persons likely to transfer property to avoid tax, and discontinued businesses.

Key distinctions: capital vs revenue receipts and expenditure; diversion of income by overriding title (not income of the assessee) vs application of income (taxable). Definitions in section 2 cover person, assessee, income and others.
concepts.analogy: Charge, period and the nature of receipts set the base.
concepts.work: A CA setting up practice on 1 July 2026 has tax year 1.7.2026 to 31.3.2027.

concepts.title: Rates of tax, surcharge, cess and marginal relief
body: Default regime (section 202) for individuals, HUFs, AOPs, BOIs and artificial juridical persons: nil up to ₹4 lakh; 5% to ₹8 lakh; 10% to ₹12 lakh; 15% to ₹16 lakh; 20% to ₹20 lakh; 25% to ₹24 lakh; 30% above, with certain exemptions and deductions foregone. Those opting out under section 202(4) use the optional regime slabs (nil to ₹2.5 lakh; 5% to ₹5 lakh; 20% to ₹10 lakh; 30% above; higher exemption for senior and very senior citizens).

Rebate under section 156 reduces tax for resident individuals with lower incomes (e.g. up to ₹60,000 under the default regime for total income up to ₹12 lakh), not available against certain special-rate income.

Surcharge applies above income thresholds; health and education cess is 4% of tax plus surcharge for all assessees. Marginal relief ensures extra tax and surcharge caused by crossing a threshold does not exceed the extra income.
concepts.analogy: Compute slab tax, then rebate, surcharge, cess and marginal relief.
concepts.work: At ₹15 lakh, default regime tax with cess is ₹1,09,200.

illustrations.q: Classify: (a) compensation received for cancellation of a business agency that was the main source of income; (b) compensation for loss of profit in a normal year; (c) a son paying, out of his salary, maintenance to his mother under a court decree; (d) a portion of family business income charged by a court decree in favour of a widow before it reaches the karta.

summary: Income-tax Act, 2025 from 1 April 2026; section 536 savings.
Default regime u/s 202; opt out u/s 202(4).
Rebate u/s 156; surcharge; 4% cess; marginal relief.
Capital vs revenue; diversion vs application.
remember: Older tax years stay under the 1961 Act.
traps: Using "previous year/assessment year" for new-Act questions.

viva.model: Repeal of the 1961 Act with savings, so proceedings and rights for tax years beginning before 1 April 2026 continue under the old Act.
The literal rule, the mischief rule and the golden rule.

viva.q: What is the tax year for a newly set-up business?
viva.model: From the date of setting up to the following 31 March.

viva.q: Distinguish diversion and application of income.
viva.model: Diversion by overriding title means income never reaches the assessee and is excluded; application means the assessee spends its own income, which remains taxable.
Relief ensuring that additional tax and surcharge on crossing a threshold do not exceed the additional income.
